item.title: CYPHER-AV: Cyber-Physical Resilience for Autonomous Vehicles
item.description:
Funding: Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV, formerly BMDV), AVF research programme, grant no. 45AVF5A011 | Lead institution: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security | Duration: 10/2024-12/2027 | Role: PI and project coordinator

Autonomous vehicles base their decisions on sensor data, so manipulating that data can lead to accidents. CYPHER-AV analyses how manipulations affect current sensors and the pipelines that process their data, and develops countermeasures. The project has three research directions: defence against physical manipulation of sensors, detection and prevention of manipulation in sensor fusion, and trustworthy processing platforms for automotive use. Results are evaluated on a demonstrator platform and are meant to serve as a reference for future research and product development.

More information:

  • BMV project page (German)
  • CISPA news item

item.title: Proseca: Proactive Security Chain for Automotive
item.description:
Funding: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK, now BMWE), grant no. 19A23009 | Lead institution: Infineon Technologies AG | Duration: 09/2023-06/2026 | Role: PI

Proseca aimed to identify security weaknesses in automotive systems proactively, before vehicles reach the field. The project addressed the security chain across components, software and the integrated vehicle.

Partners:

  • ZF Friedrichshafen AG
  • SYSGO GmbH
  • HighTec EDV-Systeme GmbH
  • Ferrous Systems GmbH
  • Fraunhofer Institute for Secure Information Technology (SIT)
  • ELEXIR AG / VEECLE GmbH (subcontractors of Infineon)

item.title: ASRIOT: Automated Security Analysis of RTOS- and MCU-based IoT Firmware
item.description:
Full title: Automatisierte Sicherheitsanalyse von RTOS und MCU basierter IoT Firmware

Funding: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF, now BMFTR) | Lead institution: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security | Duration: 04/2023-03/2026 | Role: Project coordinator and PI

Many IoT devices run firmware on microcontrollers, often based on real-time operating systems, which is difficult to analyse without the original hardware. ASRIOT developed methods to analyse such firmware automatically. The project combined emulation of firmware without the target hardware (rehosting) with fuzzing to find vulnerabilities at scale. The goal was to make security testing of MCU- and RTOS-based firmware practical for researchers and manufacturers.

item.title: KAMÄLEON: Adaptive Mobility for Light Vehicles
item.description:
Full title: Konstruktiv adaptive Mobilität bei Leichtfahrzeugen durch dynamische Fahrzeuganpassung mit KI-basierter multisensorischer Umfelderkennung

Funding: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF, now BMFTR), joint project no. 01187068 | Lead institution: HFC Human-Factors-Consult GmbH | Duration: 04/2019-12/2023 (extended, originally until 04/2022) | Role: Co-PI

KAMÄLEON investigated electric light vehicles, using tricycles as the example, that adapt to their surroundings the way a chameleon does. For instance, the maximum speed changes with the road surface, the traffic density or connecting transport. Sensors scan the surroundings, and AI methods identify the road surface and nearby road users so that the vehicle can adjust. CISPA contributed the security concept and a secure control unit, including authentication of CAN messages, to protect the vehicle’s state and approval-relevant parameters against manipulation.

Partners:

  • HFC Human-Factors-Consult GmbH (consortium lead)
  • Constin GmbH
  • OrangeBikeConcept
  • TU Braunschweig
  • Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT)
  • TÜNKERS AG
  • FH Aachen

item.title: Location Privacy in Smart Cities
item.description:
Funding: SUTD-ZJU collaboration grant | Lead institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) | Duration: 07/2017-07/2018 | Role: PI

Many location-based services reveal whether two users are close to each other, even if they do not disclose exact positions. The project studied how an attacker can exploit such proximity information to locate mobile targets. We derived analytical bounds on the number of queries an attacker needs and evaluated attacker strategies against moving targets.

Partners:

  • Zhejiang University (ZJU)

item.title: ReSILIoT: Research and Security Innovation Lab for Internet of Things
item.description:
Funding: Ministry of Defence, Singapore | Lead institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) | Duration: 09/2015-07/2018 | Role: Co-PI (own work packages and staff)

ReSILIoT investigated threats posed by and to IoT devices in enterprise and urban environments. Work included identifying IoT devices from their network and wireless traffic, detecting privacy threats from nearby devices, and observing attacks with scalable IoT honeypots. The project also developed host-based anomaly detection for resource-constrained IoT devices and testbeds for evaluating wearable devices.

item.title: NSE: National Science Experiment
item.description:
Funding: National Research Foundation, Singapore | Lead institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) | Duration: 02/2015-12/2017 | Role: Co-PI

The National Science Experiment introduced school students in Singapore to data-driven science. The team developed a wearable sensor platform within less than a year, had 50,000 units produced, and built the cloud infrastructure and a web application for exploring the data. Students carried the sensors for a week while they recorded environmental measurements, and then analysed their own data. The experiment ran in 2015, 2016 and 2017 and involved more than 94,000 students in total.

item.title: ASPIRE: Advancing Security of Public Infrastructure using Resilience and Economics
item.description:
Funding: National Research Foundation, Singapore | Lead institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) | Duration: 01/2015-07/2018 | Role: Co-PI

ASPIRE studied the security and resilience of public infrastructure, in particular water treatment, water distribution and electric power. The project combined real-world testbeds with formal attacker models and simulation of cyber-physical attacks on water distribution networks. It also organised community activities such as a competition on attack detection algorithms and gamified ICS security exercises.

item.title: CYPRO: Cyber-Physical Protection
item.description:
Funding: Ministry of Defence, Singapore | Lead institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) | Duration: 10/2014-09/2016 | Role: Co-PI (own work packages and staff)

CYPRO addressed the protection of critical infrastructure against cyber-physical attacks. The project studied attacks on industrial control systems and their effects on the physical process, as well as countermeasures such as process-aware attack detection. Experimental work used the SWaT water treatment testbed at SUTD and tools for simulating industrial networks. Results include open-source tools and datasets that are widely used in ICS security research.

item.title: SAFE: Security Assessment and Forensic Examination
item.description:
Funding: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), start-up research grant | Lead institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) | Duration: 08/2014-07/2017 | Role: PI

SAFE supported the start of my research group at SUTD. The project covered the security assessment of cyber-physical systems, in particular industrial control systems, including intrusion detection, legacy-compliant authentication of industrial traffic, malicious control logic and threat scenario testing in an electric power testbed. A second line of work addressed physical-layer security of wireless systems, such as distance bounding with ultra-wideband radios, physical-layer message integrity and GPS spoofing detection.
